title: Encryption at rest and in transit with managed keys

videos.script: The clinic's records bucket is encrypted. The dashboard says so, in green. {{green}} So are the records safe? Not from a request S3 answers. {{curl}} In your lab, an encrypted record goes to a stranger in plain text, one policy later. {{two-rows}} Encryption at rest stops somebody holding the disk. Permissions stop everybody else. {{keys}} So this lesson is about keys, and about who has to agree before data is decrypted. {{kms}} With a key the clinic manages in KMS, reading a record takes two permissions. {{bia}} You will watch KMS refuse bia, even with a bucket policy that is too broad. {{envelope}} Then the envelope: why KMS never sees your data, only small keys. {{lifecycle}} Then a key's life. Rotation, disabling, and a deletion that waits thirty days on purpose. {{transit}} And last, encryption in transit, and a bucket that refuses any request without TLS. {{end}}
